harness.execution: all Ruflo execution inside `docker run --rm` containers; no host execution; no credential paths mounted

installs_used.install-default: npm i ruflo@3.37.0, postinstall RAN, native better-sqlite3 present
installs_used.install-noscripts: npm i --ignore-scripts, better-sqlite3 sources present but UNBUILT

independent_verification_tools: md5sum / md5 (host and container shell, separate process)
recursive grep of the container filesystem from a shell that is not ruflo
find(1) on the host for filesystem side effects

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory store --key AUD_L4_SENTINEL --value 'RUFLO-L4-DURABILITY-PROBE-7f3a9c21-ZETA'  (container A, then container B: memory retrieve --key AUD_L4_SENTINEL)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Sentinel row present in .swarm/memory.db and readable from a second, brand-new container with a fresh HOME.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS. Container A exit 0, '[OK] Data stored successfully'. Container B (new container, new HOME) printed the exact value 'RUFLO-L4-DURABILITY-PROBE-7f3a9c21-ZETA', exit 0.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 (not ruflo) on /tmp/aud-ruflo-20260811/work/lane-L4/T1/repo/.swarm/memory.db: row entry_1786488210609_ca9b4d0e38fa2ade | AUD_L4_SENTINEL | default | RUFLO-L4-DURABILITY-PROBE-7f3a9c21-ZETA | semantic | 384 | unknown | active. `strings memory.db | grep -c 7f3a9c21-ZETA` = 1.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Backend actually used: SQLite via native better-sqlite3, file .swarm/memory.db, journal_mode=wal. Embedding is real: embedding_model=Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dims, float vector stored as JSON.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-nooptional>:/rf ... node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory init; memory store --key AUD_L4_SENTINEL2 --value 'RUFLO-L4-DEGRADED-PROBE-b81e44d0-OMEGA'
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Row present in .swarm/memory.db after the process exits.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: FALSE SUCCESS. init exit 0 ('Verification passed (6/6 tests)', 'Activated: 16  Failed: 7'). store exit 0, printed a result table with 'Vector: Yes (384-dim)' and '[OK] Data stored successfully'. Row does NOT exist.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 on .swarm/memory.db -> 0 rows; on .claude/memory.db -> 0 rows. ruflo's own `memory retrieve` in a fresh container: '[WARN] Key not found', exit 1. `memory list`: '[WARN] No entries found'.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: install-nooptional lacks better-sqlite3/ruvector/@huggingface/transformers; CLI announced 'Using sql.js (WASM SQLite, no build tools required)'. Also printed a swallowed error: 'Invalid PRAGMA command: wal_checkpoint(passive)'.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-noscripts>:/rf ... node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory init; memory store --key AUD_L4_SENTINEL3 --value 'RUFLO-L4-NOSCRIPTS-PROBE-c92f11ab-SIGMA'
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Row present in .swarm/memory.db after the process exits.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: FALSE SUCCESS. store exit 0, '[OK] Data stored successfully', 'Vector: Yes (384-dim)'. Row does NOT exist.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 -> 0 rows. ruflo `memory retrieve` in a fresh container -> '[WARN] Key not found'.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: This is the `npm i --ignore-scripts` install, i.e. the security-hardened default many orgs enforce. The coordinator's note that 'the CLI fully works here' holds for command surface only, not for persistence.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-noscripts>:/rf ... node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js bash -lc 'md5sum .swarm/memory.db; memory store --key SENT4 --value MECHANISM-PROBE-4d1e77-KAPPA; md5sum .swarm/memory.db; grep -rl MECHANISM-PROBE-4d1e77-KAPPA / '
scenarios.expected_postcondition: DB file bytes change; the value is findable on disk somewhere.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: store exit 0, '[OK] Data stored successfully'. md5 BEFORE = md5 AFTER = fd4c18546b2355b801019c3414b2f496 (byte-identical). A recursive grep of the ENTIRE container filesystem for the sentinel returned zero files.
scenarios.independent_verification: md5sum of the DB file computed before and after by a separate shell command; full-filesystem grep from a separate process.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Decisive mechanism evidence: the write never reaches any file. It lives only in the sql.js WASM heap and is discarded at process exit.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf ... node:24-alpine node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory init; memory store --key SENT5 --value 'ALPINE-FALLBACK-PROBE-9ac3-TAU'; memory list
scenarios.expected_postcondition: The FULLY NATIVE install (postinstall ran, better-sqlite3 compiled) should persist, as it does on node:24 glibc.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: FALSE SUCCESS on musl. init printed 'Using sql.js (WASM SQLite...)' and 'Verification passed (6/6 tests)'; store exit 0 '[OK] Data stored successfully'; memory.db md5 unchanged (dd1ba358382d46b748f3c1c317c67722 before and after); memory list -> 'No entries found'.
scenarios.independent_verification: md5sum before/after from a separate shell command; ruflo's own list in the same run.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Severity multiplier: the SAME install directory that persists correctly on node:24 loses every write on node:24-alpine. Backend selection is a silent runtime try/catch on native module load. Any glibc/musl, arch, or corrupted-build mismatch converts a working install into a silent data-loss install with no error and no exit-code change.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-noscripts>:/rf ... node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory store --key TAILERED_L4 --value 'TAILERED-REPO-DURABILITY-3ce9d1'  (run against a copy of the coordinator's already-`ruflo init`ed Tailered repo)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Row present in the Tailered checkout's .swarm/memory.db.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: FALSE SUCCESS. exit 0, '[OK] Data stored successfully'. memory.db md5 unchanged (77851703116d7332230222d5662894df before and after); 0 rows.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host md5 + host sqlite3 on the copied Tailered repo at /tmp/aud-ruflo-20260811/work/lane-L4/T13repo.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Reproduces on the actual Tailered repository layout, not just a synthetic project.

scenarios.command: code read: @claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory/memory-initializer.js :: verifyMemoryInit (line 2264)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A durability self-check should write, close, reopen from disk in a fresh handle, and read back.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: verifyMemoryInit loads the file into a single in-memory sql.js image, INSERTs, SELECTs the same in-memory image, and never calls db.export() or re-opens the file. It cannot observe the failure in S02-S06 and prints 'Verification passed (6/6 tests)'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Static read of the shipped dist code; corroborated empirically by S02 and S05 where 6/6 passed while storage was a total no-op.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Canonical 'Ruflo verifying Ruflo' trap: the product's own health signal is structurally blind to its worst failure mode.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory init  (fully native install, linux/arm64, node v24.19.0)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: exit 0 with a completion summary.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: Process ABORTS: 'node[1]: void node::RemoveEnvironmentCleanupHook(...) Assertion failed: (env) != nullptr' with a native stack in agentdb/node_modules/better-sqlite3/build/Release/better_sqlite3.node (Statement::~Statement). Exit code 133. No success summary printed.
scenarios.independent_verification: Exit code captured without a pipe. Host sqlite3 afterwards: 34 tables present, pragma integrity_check = ok, metadata rows written.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: The abort happens at interpreter teardown AFTER the work committed, so the DB is actually fine. The user sees a hard crash and no confirmation. Inverse of the S02 class: real postcondition, reported failure.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory stats  (clean repo, fully native install)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A statistics table.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: Same native assertion abort, exit 133, reproducible on a clean, uncorrupted repo. No statistics ever printed.
scenarios.independent_verification: Exit code captured directly; repeated on two different repos (T1 clean, T10 corrupted).
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: `memory stats` is REACHABLE but never EFFECTIVE on this platform. The same command works on the sql.js path (which is the path that loses data).

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory store --key KILLK$i ... launched in background, SIGKILL (kill -9) at t+3s, repeated 6x, then independent read
scenarios.expected_postcondition: No partial rows; DB remains valid; a completed store survives.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: 5 of 6 attempts SIGKILLed (wait status 137) wrote nothing. 1 attempt that completed before the kill window (KILLK4) persisted. pragma integrity_check = ok. No stray *.lock, *.tmp, or *.agentdb.lock files left behind. memory.db-wal truncated to 0 bytes.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 pragma integrity_check + row listing; host `find` for lock/temp residue.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: The native better-sqlite3/WAL path is crash-atomic. Forced termination is loud (exit 137) and produces no false success.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i --read-only --tmpfs /tmp -v <install-default>:/rf:ro -v <repo>:/repo:ro ... memory store --key ROSENT --value READONLY-PROBE-11ff
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Loud failure, non-zero exit, nothing written.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: LOUD FAILURE. exit 1. '[ERROR] memory database has an active native WAL connection (found -wal/-shm sidecar files) - refusing an unsafe sql.js whole-image write. ... Bridge unavailable: attempt to write a readonly database'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3: only the two pre-existing rows, no ROSENT.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Note the asymmetry that explains RUF-401: the #2735 guard refuses the sql.js whole-image write only when -wal/-shm sidecars exist. In a repo that has never had a native writer (no sidecars) the same fallback accepts the write silently and drops it.

scenarios.command: python3 truncate ruvector.db 1589248 -> 4096 bytes; then docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory list
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A diagnostic naming the corrupt file, or graceful degradation.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: UNRECOVERABLE ABORT. Rust panic: "thread '<unnamed>' panicked at redb-2.6.3/src/tree_store/page_store/page_manager.rs:243:9: assertion failed: storage.raw_file_len()? >= header.layout().len()" then 'fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic ... aborting'. Exit 133. Same for `memory store`. No file name, no recovery hint.
scenarios.independent_verification: Exit code captured directly; reproduced for two different subcommands; recovered by restoring the file from a copy.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: ruvector.db is a 1.5 MB redb binary that `ruflo init` writes into the REPOSITORY ROOT. Any truncation (partial clone, LFS mishap, interrupted write, editor) hard-DoSes every memory command, including read-only ones. There is no `memory repair` path and no ruflo command survives to run one.

scenarios.command: python3 overwrite 2048 bytes at offset 200000 of .swarm/memory.db (pragma integrity_check now reports 'Tree 50 page 50: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11'); then docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory list; memory store --key CORRUPTK2
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A warning that the store is damaged, or a refusal.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: SILENT. `memory list` exit 0, rendered the entry table normally. `memory store` exit 0, '[OK] Data stored successfully', and the new row WAS written into the corrupt image. integrity_check still fails afterwards. No warning at any point.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 pragma integrity_check before and after; host sqlite3 row listing.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Ruflo never validates database integrity and will keep appending to a structurally corrupt store.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js 6 x `memory store --key CONC$i` launched simultaneously in one container, then independent read
scenarios.expected_postcondition: All 6 rows durable, DB valid, or loud contention errors.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: All 6 reported '[OK] Data stored successfully'; all 6 rows present; pragma integrity_check = ok.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 row listing + integrity check.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Native path only. The shipped source documents the opposite hazard for the sql.js path (memory-initializer.js #2878: an unlocked concurrent whole-image write 'flushes a predecessor image over it and silently drops the new row'); not separately reproduced here because that path drops writes unconditionally (S02-S06).

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory search -q 'durability probe'
scenarios.expected_postcondition: The stored sentinel is returned with a similarity score.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS. 'Found 1 results', AUD_L4_SENTINEL, score 0.71, search time 87ms.
scenarios.independent_verification: Cross-checked against the independently-read embedding column: embedding_model=Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, embedding_dimensions=384, real float vector.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-noscripts>:/rf ... node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory store --key S1 --value 'authentication patterns for oauth login'; memory search -q 'oauth authentication'; memory stats
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Either results, or a loud statement that semantic search is unavailable.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: SILENT DEGRADATION. store exit 0 '[OK]'. search exit 0 -> '[WARN] No results found'. stats exit 0 -> reports 'Provider: Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2', 'Dimensions: 384', 'Semantic Search: yes', and prints 'V3 Performance: 150x-12,500x faster search with HNSW indexing'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3: the DB contains zero entries, so there is nothing for search to find; the capability report is decoupled from reality.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: The status surface asserts a working embedding provider and semantic search on an install where nothing is stored at all.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory backup
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A snapshot file that an independent reader can open and that contains the live rows.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS. 'Backed up -> /repo/.swarm/backups/memory-2026-08-11T23-09-44-675Z.db, Size: 668 KB, Rotated: 0'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 on the snapshot: pragma integrity_check = ok, select count(*) from memory_entries = 8, matching the live DB.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: This is the one persistence claim in the memory subsystem that verified cleanly end to end on the native path.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory store ...  (any memory subcommand)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A memory write only.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: Every memory subcommand prints '[INFO] Started Ruflo background daemon for /repo' and creates .claude-flow/daemon.pid, .claude-flow/daemon-state.json, .claude-flow/logs/daemon.log, .claude-flow/metrics/codebase-map.json, .claude-flow/policy/state.json, ruvector.db (repo root), and $HOME/.claude-flow/update-state.json. The daemon schedules 7 recurring workers (map 15m, audit 10m, optimize 15m, consolidate 30m, testgaps 20m, backup 24h, harness 6h) with ttl 12h and idle shutdown 30m.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host `find` of the repo and the mounted HOME before/after; host read of daemon-state.json and daemon.log.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: No prompt, no flag, no --no-daemon on the store command. Directly conflicts with the Tailered invariant that an external process agent must not mutate the company repo. Also note daemon-state.json config.workers includes a 'harness' worker described as 'Self-optimizing harness loop (opt-in RUFLO_HARNESS_LOOP, $0-default)' and an aiWorkersEnabled flag.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js daemon status  (run in a fresh container after the writer container was destroyed)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Correctly reports that no daemon is running.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: Correct: 'Status: STOPPED'. But the persisted .claude-flow/daemon-state.json still contains "running": true with a stale PID (37) from the destroyed container.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host read of daemon-state.json vs ruflo's own status output.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: The reader liveness-checks the PID, so the stale record is contained today. It is still a durable false statement in a file, and PID-based liveness is unreliable across container/host boundaries where a low PID from a container can collide with a live host process.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js autopilot enable; autopilot config --max-iterations 4; autopilot check x N (each in a separate process)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Iteration counter and history survive process exit and advance monotonically.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS. .claude-flow/data/autopilot-state.json and autopilot-log.json written via writeFileAtomic. Across 3 separate processes: iterations 1, 2, 3; history array grew to 3 entries with {ts, iteration, completed, total}. A later run reached 'CONTINUE: 2/2 tasks remaining (iteration 4/4)' then 'ALLOW STOP: Max iterations (4) reached' then 'ALLOW STOP: Autopilot disabled'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host read of .claude-flow/data/autopilot-state.json between invocations, parsed with python3.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Autopilot checkpointing is genuinely durable and a terminal state exists (max-iterations, timeout, disabled).

scenarios.command: write a truncated/invalid JSON into .claude-flow/swarm-tasks.json, then docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js autopilot check
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A loud parse error, or CONTINUE (fail-safe).
scenarios.observed_postcondition: FAIL-OPEN. 'ALLOW STOP: No tasks discovered from any source', exit 0. The same message is produced when the queue is genuinely empty. With zero sources, `autopilot status` reports 'Tasks: 0/0 (100%)'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host-side corruption of the input file; ruflo's own output compared against the known 2 pending tasks that were in the file moments earlier.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: An unreadable work queue is indistinguishable from a completed one, and the completion signal is 100%. For a tool whose headline claim is 'keeps agents working until ALL tasks are done', a corrupt queue silently means 'done'.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js workflow run -t development --task 'probe task'
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A checkpoint that a later process can list, resume, or reap.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: A checkpoint IS written to .claude-flow/workflows/store.json with status 'running', steps[0].status 'pending', createdAt/startedAt. The process then exits immediately; nothing executes and no terminal status is ever written. Two such records accumulated as permanent zombie 'running' workflows.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host read of .claude-flow/workflows/store.json after the container was destroyed.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Checkpointing exists (contrary to a 'no persistence at all' reading), but there is no execution and no terminal-state writer on the run path. A crashed or credential-less run leaves an indefinitely 'running' record.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js workflow list   (with 2 records present in store.json)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Both workflows listed.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: '[INFO] No workflows found', exit 0. Root cause read from the shipped code: commands/workflow.js:276-278 sends `status: status || 'all'` to the workflow_list MCP tool, and mcp-tools/workflow-tools.js filters with `w.status === input.status`, so the default sentinel 'all' is applied as a literal equality filter and can never match.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host read of store.json proving the records exist; `workflow list --status running` and `--status failed` each returned exactly 1 workflow, confirming the store is readable and the default filter is the defect.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: The default inventory view of the workflow subsystem is unconditionally empty. A zombie workflow is invisible unless the operator already knows its exact status string.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js workflow list --status running
scenarios.expected_postcondition: A row with ID, template, progress, start time.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: Row rendered with empty ID, empty Template, 'undefined%' progress, and 'Invalid Date'. The tool returns workflowId/createdAt while the table declares columns id/template/progress/startedAt.
scenarios.independent_verification: Direct comparison of the tool's documented return shape in mcp-tools/workflow-tools.js against the column keys in commands/workflow.js.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js workflow stop <id>
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Terminal state persisted.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS. '[OK] Workflow ... stopped'; store.json record became status 'failed', steps[0].status 'skipped', error 'Stopped by user', completedAt set. The second workflow remained 'running'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host read of store.json parsed with python3 after the container exited.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: A terminal state is reachable, but only by explicit operator action against an ID that `workflow list` will not show them.

scenarios.command: node probe driving @claude-flow/cli/dist/src/services/policy-runtime.js directly (bypasses the CLI's TTY gate): setPolicyMode('enforce'); setPolicyBudget({id:'cap5',maxCostUsd:5,periodMs:86400000}); upsertPolicyRule(allow model.call); then 52 evaluatePolicyRequest calls at costUsd 0.1 across 3 separate node processes
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Spend is capped at 5.00 before the 51st call; usage survives process exit.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS on the mechanism. Process 1: 40 allowed, usage.costUsd 4.000000000000002. Process 2 (new process): 9 allowed, usage 4.899999999999999. Process 3: 1 allowed then 2 denied with reason 'budget-exceeded:cap5', final usage 4.999999999999998. A single costUsd:1000 request was denied pre-flight.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host read of .claude-flow/policy/state.json between processes; each spend batch ran in its own node process.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: The policy engine's budget IS a genuine pre-decision check (engine.js applyBudget runs before the allow, consumeBudget after) and IS durable across processes.

scenarios.command: same probe, inspecting usage.costUsd accumulation
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Exact ledger arithmetic (Tailered requires integer micro-dollars).
scenarios.observed_postcondition: IEEE-754 float accumulation: 4.000000000000002 after 40 x 0.1; 4.899999999999999; 4.999999999999998. engine.js consumeBudget does `usage.costUsd += request.action.costUsd ?? 0` on JS numbers; maxCostUsd is a float too.
scenarios.independent_verification: Values read from the on-disk policy state file by a separate process (python3/host cat), not from ruflo's own report.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Violates Tailered invariant 'deterministic code owns money'. The enforced ceiling is approximate; drift is signed and unbounded over a long window, and the final total 4.999999999999998 shows the cap can be undershot or overshot by accumulated epsilon.

scenarios.command: same probe, evaluatePolicyRequest with NO costUsd on the action
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Deny (cannot meter, cannot cap).
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS. outcome denied, enforcedOutcome denied, reason 'budget-metering-required:cap5:costUsd'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Decision object read directly from the engine's return value in a standalone process.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Fail-closed on unmetered actions is correct design.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js policy status  (fresh repo, and after `ruflo init` in the coordinator's trial repo)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Some default ceiling, or an explicit statement that none exists.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: Default state is {"mode":"legacy","rules":[],"budgets":[],"usage":[],"approvals":[],"receipts":[]}. engine.js maps mode ranks legacy=0, observe=1, enforce=2, and every budget violation returns enforcedOutcome 'allowed' unless mode === 'enforce'.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host read of .claude-flow/policy/state.json; corroborated by the file ruflo wrote unprompted during S18.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Out of the box Ruflo has NO cost ceiling: no budgets, and a mode in which budget violations are recorded but not enforced.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js policy budget set '{...maxCostUsd:5...}'  and the same with `docker run -t`
scenarios.expected_postcondition: The budget is configured.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: REFUSED in both non-TTY and stdout-only-TTY runs: '[ERROR] policy administration requires an interactive local terminal'. commands/policy.js:18 requires `process.stdin.isTTY && process.stdout.isTTY`. state.json unchanged (budgets: []).
scenarios.independent_verification: Host read of state.json after each attempt confirmed no mutation.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Deliberate anti-self-authorization control, but the consequence is that the only cost ceiling Ruflo has cannot be configured from CI, a container, a Dockerfile, a provisioning script, or any headless agent session. A fully-interactive-TTY path was not reachable from this audit harness (no pty available); that the control works WITH a real pty is UNKNOWN.

scenarios.command: code read: @claude-flow/cli/dist/src/services/headless-worker-executor.js and mcp-client.js
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Model spend is authorized against the budget BEFORE the call.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: headless-worker-executor.js -- the component that spawns model-backed workers -- contains ZERO references to the policy engine (grep for evaluatePolicyRequest/authorizeMcpTool/policy: no matches). Cost is extracted POST-hoc from the result envelope at line 371 (`costUsd: numOrUndef(obj.total_cost_usd ?? obj.cost_usd ?? obj.totalCostUsd)`). The only policy call site is mcp-client.js:234 for outbound MCP tool calls, and its attributes come from classifyMcpTool(), which returns only {actionType, network, destructive, namespaceAccess} and never costUsd.
scenarios.independent_verification: Static grep of the shipped dist across the whole cli package; cross-checked against the empirical S28 result that a costUsd-less request is denied as 'budget-metering-required'.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Decisive for Tailered invariants 11-14. There is no reserve-and-settle: the budget engine can only be fed a caller-declared estimate, the actual spender never consults it, and the real number arrives after the money is gone. With a cost budget configured in enforce mode, MCP tool calls would ALSO be denied wholesale as unmetered.

scenarios.command: same probe: verifyPolicyLedger after 10 receipts
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Tamper-evident receipt chain.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS. {"valid":true,"length":10}. engine.js verifyLedger checks sequence, previousReceiptHash linkage, payload hash, and receiptId derivation; optional HMAC signing when a key is configured.
scenarios.independent_verification: Ledger verified from a separate node process reading the on-disk state file.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Hash-chained receipts are real. Note the chain and the state it protects live in the same repo-local JSON file that the agent under governance can write.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory store --key K0 --value V0  (before `memory init`)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Non-zero exit on failure.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: PASS. '[ERROR] Database not initialized. Run: claude-flow memory init', exit 1.

scenarios.observed_postcondition: {"distPath":"/rf/node_modules/@claude-flow/memory/dist/index.js","version":"3.0.0-alpha.22","resolvedBy":"init","resolvedAt":"..."}. The absolute path of the machine that ran init is baked into a repo file.

scenarios.command: host inspection after `memory init` on the sql.js path
scenarios.expected_postcondition: One authoritative database.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: TWO databases: .swarm/memory.db and .claude/memory.db, byte-identical at creation (both fd4c18546b2355b801019c3414b2f496 in T4). init prints 'Synced to: /repo/.claude/memory.db'. Subsequent writes target .swarm only.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host md5sum of both files.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: A second copy that is written once and then never maintained is a divergence trap for anyone who reads the wrong one.

scenarios.command: host sqlite3 read of the metadata table after a native-backend session
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Metadata reflects the backend actually in use.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: metadata contains sql_js|true even in the run where the CLI printed 'Using native better-sqlite3' and better-sqlite3 demonstrably performed the writes (S01). The value is written at schema creation and never reconciled.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 `select * from metadata` compared against the CLI's own backend banner in the same run.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: The database's own record of which engine wrote it is wrong, which is exactly the field a post-incident investigation of RUF-401 would reach for.

scenarios.command: docker run --rm -i -v <install-default>:/rf -v <repo>:/repo -v <home>:/root -w /repo -e HOME=/root node:24 node /rf/node_modules/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js memory store -k 'DOCEXAMPLE' -v 'the-intended-value-QQQ'  (the form printed in `ruflo memory --help` EXAMPLES)
scenarios.expected_postcondition: Stores the value.
scenarios.observed_postcondition: -v binds to --verbose, not --value. Flags parsed as {"key":"DOCEXAMPLE","verbose":true,...} and the intended value survives only as a positional. The row stored correctly ('the-intended-value-QQQ') but the command silently switched into DEBUG output mode.
scenarios.independent_verification: Host sqlite3 read of the stored content plus the CLI's own [DEBUG] Flags dump.
scenarios.label: VERIFIED
scenarios.notes: Works by accident today. A value that begins with '-' would be consumed as a flag. The tool's own help text teaches the ambiguous form.

scenarios.command: code read: @claude-flow/cli/dist/src/memory/memory-bridge.js getDb() comment block
scenarios.observed_postcondition: The shipped source documents that agentdb's EmbeddingService 'silently falls back to MOCK EMBEDDINGS (random vectors)' when its transformers path fails, and ships a monkey-patch to rescue it. The rescue is itself conditional on ruvector being available -- a package ABSENT from install-nooptional.
scenarios.independent_verification: Static read only. Not reproduced here: on the installs where this path is reachable, S02/S03 showed nothing persists at all, so the embedding quality is moot.
scenarios.label: INFERRED
scenarios.notes: A third silent-degradation channel in the same subsystem: search that returns confident, meaningless results rather than none.
